audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Tryndamere levels 2, 3 and first item and Skill at 4-5 and 6, while every why for those rows describes a Nautilus takeover and the win rate is 56.25%.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Tryndamere. Before Fury and crit items he has no answer to a hook into root.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Skill, Nautilus x5, Tryndamere with ratings to match.

audit.why: Spikes: levels 2-3 short trades before Fury, level 6 Depth Charge, first item engage, 2+ items his crit takeover. Undying Rage and Depth Charge share a 120/100/80 cooldown, so the ult trade is one-for-one.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described as a plain slow ('W slow plus dropback', 'W dropback'), which loses the only counterplay in it, and the Bloodlust heal is never tied to Grievous Wounds despite the flagged interaction.
audit.why: Riot text: Mocking Shout (850 range, 14s) drops surrounding champions' attack damage, and 'Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced'. Bloodlust (12s) consumes Fury to heal him.
audit.corrected: Walk toward him rather than turning to run and Mocking Shout costs you AD but no move speed. Grievous Wounds before any extended trade, and track Spinning Slash at 8-12s as his only gap-close.

edits.before: Level 1 is roughly even — I have no all-in without W or E yet, though my passive root on first auto makes any auto-trade favorable. From Level 2-3 I take over: I land Dredge Line to yank Tryndamere into my passive root, drop Riptide for the slow, and my Titan's Wrath shield plus splash burn wins the short trade outright before his Battle Fury rage is built and his spin actually hurts. Don't chuck Q at max range into a creep — land it on him, and never let him build rage off free short autos on me.
edits.after: Level 1 is roughly even — you have no all-in without W or E yet, though your passive root on the first auto makes any auto-trade favorable. From Level 2-3 you take over: land Dredge Line to yank Tryndamere into that root, drop Riptide for the slow, and Titan's Wrath plus splash burn wins the short trade outright before his Battle Fury is built and Spinning Slash actually hurts. Do not chuck Q at max range into a creep — land it on him, and never feed Fury with free short autos.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay mine as my W shield and E waves scale — I control the wave and zone him off farm, and every time he steps up to spin a trade I can Q-pull-root-E him and come out ahead. Level 6 is my hardest spike: Depth Charge is a homing, undodgeable knock-up, so I chain R into Q-pull and lock him through his E gap-close and W dropback — that's a guaranteed kill setup or a free gank. The one thing to respect is letting him stack rage; commit while his spin is still weak, not after he's farmed it up.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours as the W shield and E waves scale — you control the wave and zone him off farm, and every time he steps up to spin you Q-pull, root and E him for the better trade. Level 6 is your hardest spike: Depth Charge is homing and point-click, so R into Q-pull locks him through Spinning Slash's 8-12s gap-close — a guaranteed kill setup or a free gank. Respect only his Fury; commit while the spin is still weak, not after he has farmed it up.

edits.before: This is where it flips. Once Tryndamere has crit and lifesteal items, Undying Rage means my whole CC chain — root, Q, R, E slow — locks him but can't kill him, and he survives at 1 HP for 5 seconds then spins my low tank damage down while I'm on cooldown. My base damage doesn't scale; his does. So I close this lane on my Level 6 and first-item windows, then stop trying to solo-duel him and pivot to teamfights, where my Depth Charge picks his carries and my CC chain peels for mine instead of feeding his reset spin.
edits.after: This is where it flips. Once Tryndamere has crit and lifesteal items, Undying Rage means your whole CC chain — root, Q, R, E slow — locks him but cannot kill him: he lives at 1 HP, then spins your low tank damage down while you are on cooldown. Your base damage does not scale; his does. So close the lane on your Level 6 and first-item windows, stop trying to solo-duel him, and pivot to teamfights where Depth Charge picks his carries and your chain peels for yours.

notes: Content early/mid/late were written in first person and are converted to second person at matched length. The most usable new fact is Mocking Shout's condition: it only slows targets whose backs are turned, so walking at him beats walking away.
